 7-foot-5 center Cherif Millogo commits to Kentucky
 Jack Pilgrim 1h 1 Share Share 
 Mark Pope has landed his biggest recruit to date—literally! Cherif Millogo , a 7-foot-5 center and one of the best prospects in 2027, has committed to Kentucky.
 The No. 11 overall recruit and No. 2 center chose UK on Wednesday over offers from BYU, USC, Arkansas, Louisville, North Carolina, Tennessee, Arizona and Texas, among others. He took his first official visit to Lexington on October 10, then made trips to BYU and USC on Oct. 28 and 31, respectively.
 Millogo gives the Wildcats a second pledge in the class alongside top-30 recruit Ryan Hampton , who joined the fold back in June. 
 Standing 7-foot-5 and weighing 250 pounds, the future five-star has a real chance to close out the 2027 cycle as a top-10 talent—and could climb into the top five, assuming he stays healthy and produces at the level he’s capable of in his senior campaign at St. Francis in La Canada Flintridge, CA. He’s the most physically imposing big man in the country, agile for his size and capable of knocking down jump shots, but also an impossible load to handle in the frontcourt. Boasting a 7-foot-9 wingspan, Millogo is a vicious rim protector with tremendous upside as he improves his strength and conditioning and continues stacking game reps.
 Kentucky also offered Lewis Uvwo, Darius Wabbington, and Paul Osaruyi among ’27 centers, but zeroed in on Millogo entering the fall, quietly bringing him to campus while also moving to hire Alfred Aboya, formerly of NBA Academy Africa, whose connections to the top-15 talent—among many others—run deep. Millogo, a native of Burkina Faso in West Africa, lives with his guardian and agent, former UCLA star and longtime NBA player Luc Mbah a Moute, who was Aboya’s roommate and best friend with the Bruins during their run of three straight Final Fours in Westwood.
 Pope gets the job done with arguably the nation’s most intriguing high school talent.
